title: All-Scope Full-Text Search Baseline
summary: give every Docs Viewer scope Studio's current full-text field policy before considering further search improvements
content_html:
All-Scope Full-Text Search Baseline

Status

The common baseline is complete and closed after explicit user approval. All five configured working indexes use title, heading, body, and code; focused policy and lifecycle contracts pass; and representative parent and hosted-child queries resolve through the shared browser query path. The exact Search-only Analysis delta was explicitly published on 2026-08-14, leaving working and public Search identical.

Purpose

Every configured Docs Viewer scope now uses the full-text Search baseline already shipped for Studio. All scopes share one v2 index producer and browser query path; the former Analysis, Notes, Processing, and Dotlineform metadata-only exception has been removed.

SM-1 — Studio Full-Text Search Delivery established the reusable extraction and ranking contract. DSI-2 — Scope-Level Sub-Scope Search Delivery added eligible visibly hosted sub-scope documents to the same atomic scope index. The combined parent and sub-scope corpora now provide enough content to make full text the common baseline before any further Search improvement is considered.

This is a policy alignment, not a new search feature or a separate Analysis experiment.

Common Baseline

Every configured Docs Viewer scope adopts exactly:

"search_fields": ["title", "heading", "body", "code"]

The existing shared behavior remains unchanged:

  • title matches rank above heading matches, which rank above body and authored-code matches;
  • doc_id, URL, update date, parent identity, parent title, sub-scope identity, and collection title remain structural or display metadata and do not emit postings;
  • visible headings, prose, inline code, and fenced code come from the shared Markdown extraction boundary;
  • front matter, report declarations, link destinations, media paths, raw configuration, scripts, styles, and excluded documents do not contribute searchable terms;
  • each scope owns one complete atomic index containing its eligible parent documents and eligible visibly hosted sub-scope documents; and
  • exact {scope, sub_scope, doc_id} identity and the active-route resolver continue to own child navigation.

There is no scope-name branch, second schema, alternate tokenizer, independent child index, or browser-side result merger. New Docs Viewer scopes should start from this same field policy unless a deliberate exception is approved.

Delivery

  • [x] Change Analysis, Notes, Processing, and Dotlineform to the same search_fields policy as Studio.
  • [x] Make the full-text policy the default for newly created Docs Viewer scopes.
  • [x] Explicitly rebuild the complete working Search index for every configured scope. Ordinary document saves remain Docs-only.
  • [x] Confirm every generated index declares only title, heading, body, and code posting fields and retains exact parent/sub-scope membership and routing identity.
  • [x] Run a small representative title, heading, prose, and code query set for each scope, including visibly hosted Analysis and Dotlineform child results.
  • [x] Inspect document, term, posting, and raw-byte counts for obvious regressions without introducing per-scope budgets or optimization work.
  • [x] Preview and explicitly Publish the Analysis Search delta through the existing public Publish boundary. The accepted Search-only delta changed no documents, exclusions, media, or document-location products.

The baseline is complete: all configured working indexes and the accepted Analysis public projection use the same full-text field policy. Local and external-local scopes require no public projection step.

Deliberate Omissions

This baseline does not change relevance weights, prefix behavior, snippets, highlighting, phrase search, stemming, synonyms, typo handling, query language, section results, deep links, cross-scope Search, or Search presentation. It does not change parent Index or Recent composition.

Catalogue Search remains a separate domain-owned system and is not a Docs Viewer scope.

Search improvements should be considered only after this common baseline is implemented, rebuilt, published where required, and accepted.

Closeout

Completed and closed 2026-08-14 after explicit user approval. The accepted result is one shared full-text field policy across Studio, Analysis, Notes, Processing, and Dotlineform, including eligible visibly hosted sub-scope documents and exact structured child navigation. Analysis working and public Search are byte-identical at 266 documents, 2,663 terms, and 354,633 bytes; the accepted Publish changed only site/assets/data/search/analysis/index.json and left documents, exclusions, document locations, media, and Catalogue follow-through unchanged.

Docs Viewer Search and Docs Viewer Search Index own the durable current state. This document remains as the bounded field-policy and publication record; the earlier concept and delivery records remain retained evidence. No relevance, presentation, Catalogue Search, cross-scope Search, or retirement work began during closeout. SM-2 — Docs Viewer Search Relevance Delivery remains proposed and unstarted.

Closeout-only verification targeted the six affected Studio documents with registered media builds skipped: 241 documents emitted with zero payload writes, removals, derived-index writes, or warnings. The Studio Search index rebuilt after the closeout wording changed and then skipped an identical repeat. Eleven affected generated JSON files parsed successfully; Analysis working and public Search retained matching SHA-256 a6586ba1739c9faad924125b448e4b3a7a7210278c034d1cf56e43a2b9299035; and git diff --check passed. The accepted 86 focused implementation checks were not rerun during documentation-only closeout, and no browser check was added or run.

Relationships

Docs Viewer Search and Docs Viewer Search Index remain the durable current-state authorities. SM-1 owns the shared full-text extraction and ranking implementation. DSI-2 owns combined parent/sub-scope corpus membership and exact child routing. This document owns only the remaining all-scope field-policy alignment.
